entries.description: since AlexNet beat conventional computer vision models on ImageNet
entries.subject: since AlexNet
entries.object: conventional computer vision models on ImageNet

spans.text: Ever since AlexNet (:numref:`sec_alexnet`) beat conventional computer vision models on ImageNet, it has become popular to construct very deep networks by stacking blocks of convolutions, all designed according to the same pattern.

entries.task_id: googlenet|added|multiple branches of different convolution width
entries.description: GoogLeNet added multiple branches of different convolution width
entries.subject: GoogLeNet
entries.object: multiple branches of different convolution width

spans.text: GoogLeNet (:numref:`sec_googlenet`) added multiple branches of different convolution width, combining the advantages of VGG and NiN in its Inception block.
Almost a decade later, the ResNet design is still popular, a testament to its design.
Lastly, ResNeXt (:numref:`subsec_resnext`) added grouped convolutions, offering a better trade-off between parameters and computation.
We chose to do so since their cost is usually enormous, relying on brute-force search, genetic algorithms, reinforcement learning, or some other form of hyperparameter optimization.

spans.text: In the following we discuss an idea that is quite different to the quest for the *single best network*.
It is computationally relatively inexpensive, it leads to scientific insights on the way, and it is quite effective in terms of the quality of outcomes.
